entities.summary:
Intel Corporation is an American multinational semiconductor corporation founded in 1968 by Gordon Moore and Robert Noyce in Mountain View, California. The world's largest semiconductor manufacturer by revenue through most of the personal computer era, Intel's x86 processor architecture has powered the majority of the world's computers for five decades.

Intel invented the microprocessor in 1971 (Intel 4004), enabling the personal computer revolution. Its 1978 8086 processor created the x86 instruction set architecture that still runs most of the world's computers, servers, and data centers. Moore's Law — co-founder Gordon Moore's 1965 observation that transistor density doubles every two years — became both a technological roadmap and a self-fulfilling prophecy that guided semiconductor investment for 50 years.

Intel's Wintel duopoly with Microsoft dominated personal computing through the 1980s-2000s. The late 2010s saw AMD challenge Intel's process leadership, and Apple's transition of Macs to Apple Silicon in 2020 threatened Intel's premium laptop market. More significantly, NVIDIA's GPU architecture eclipsed Intel's CPUs for AI computing. Intel's struggles to advance its manufacturing process nodes put it behind TSMC and Samsung, prompting a return to manufacturing investment under CEO Pat Gelsinger and massive government subsidies under the US CHIPS Act.
